Part I

Getting into the system

Everyone signs in at the same address. What you see afterwards depends on the role your administrator gave your account.

1

Signing in

Open the system in a browser and enter the email address and password you were issued. Passwords are personal — change yours under Profile after your first sign-in.

  1. Type your college email address, for example nina.reyes@sfxc.edu.
  2. Type your password. The eye button at the end of the field shows what you typed; press it again to hide it.
  3. Tick Remember me on this computer if this is your own computer. Next time the email address is filled in for you, and your browser may offer to save the password itself. Leave it unticked on a shared computer.
  4. Choose Sign In. The system opens the page you work with most. A Fund Officer lands on Fund Availability, a Reviewer on Reviewer, and so on.
About the demo panel

While the college is still testing, the sign-in page can list demo accounts and their passwords so testers can pick one. The list starts folded under Demo Accounts; choose Show to open it, then pick an account to fill the form. The list folds away again so Sign In is back in view. Anyone who opens the page can still read the accounts. Before the system carries real requests, an administrator should switch the panel off — see A6.

2

The dashboard

The dashboard counts every request you are allowed to see, grouped by the stage it has reached. Choosing a tile opens the list behind it; View Details on any row expands the request, and for an approved or completed request it also shows the disbursement voucher with every approving code and date recorded so far.

If a tile is the stage you act on, it reads Open action queue and takes you straight to your work page instead: Pending Fund for the Fund Officer, Pending Review for the Reviewer, Pending Endorsement for the Endorser, and Pending Approval for the JCA and JMAPC Chairs.

Once a request has been endorsed, its list shows a Final Approver column reading JMAPC or JCA, so you can see whose desk it is waiting on.

Counts are taken from the database rather than from the rows on screen, so a tile stays accurate even when the list below it shows only the most recent page of requests.

3

Roles and what each one sees

A request cannot skip a stage, and no one can act out of turn: a page only lists the requests that are currently waiting on that role.

RoleActs atCan see
RequestorCreates the requestRequests from their own department
Fund OfficerFund availability, then the voucherAll departments
ReviewerReviewAll departments
EndorserEndorsementAll departments
JCA ChairFinal approval, when endorsed to JCAAll departments
JMAPC ChairFinal approval, when endorsed to JMAPCAll departments
AdministratorSettings and recordsEverything
4

The request window

Whichever stage you work at, opening a request from your queue shows the same window, built from three cards of the same width, top to bottom.

CardWhat it holds
Disbursement VoucherThe voucher as it stands, with every approving code recorded so far. Print and Download Excel sit at the top right of this card, beside the voucher number — the Fund Officer also sees Save Voucher there while checking funds.
Comments, Notes and RemarksEvery remark written on the request so far, oldest first, with who wrote it, at which stage, and when.
Your DecisionYour part: the attachments, the decision, a Remarks box, and the button that submits it at the bottom right. The badge in the corner names your role.
Sending a request back

Reviewers, Endorsers and Final Approvers can send a request back one stage instead of deciding on it. Remarks are required when you do, because they are how the previous person learns what to fix. A request that is sent back is not given an approving code.

Close at the top right of the window stays in view however far you scroll.

Part II

The approval workflow, stage by stage

The seven stages below are a fixed sequence. Each one ends by handing the request to the next role, and every approval is stamped with a code and a timestamp that stay on the voucher.

1CreateFOR_FUND_AVAILABILITY
2Fund checkFOR_REVIEW
3ReviewFOR_ENDORSEMENT
4EndorseFOR_APPROVAL
5ApproveAPPROVED
6VoucherAPPROVED
7CompleteCOMPLETED
Stage 1

Create the request

Requestor

Choose Make Request in the sidebar. The date, the control number, your department and your name are filled in for you and cannot be edited — the control number is issued by the system in the form YYYYMMDD-SFXC-00001.

  1. Enter the Amount in pesos.
  2. Write the Particulars of Request — what the money is for, in a sentence an approver outside your department will understand.
  3. Attach Pre-Approval Notes if the request was already discussed: one image or PDF, up to 2 MB.
  4. Add Attachments — quotations, invoices, supporting papers. Up to 2 MB each.
  5. Submit. The request moves to the Fund Officer.
Stage 2

Confirm the funds

Fund Officer

New requests appear under Fund Availability. Choose Review Funds to open the request together with a draft of its disbursement voucher.

  1. On the voucher, pick the sub-account the money will come from. The voucher's Fund Type and Fund Name fill in from your choice, and the Fund Account box in the Your Decision card repeats it.
  2. Correct Pay to, Address, Voucher No. or the particulars on the voucher if they need to differ from the request, then choose Save Voucher at the top of the voucher card. This is the only stage at which those details can be changed.
  3. Set Availability to Available or Not Available.
  4. Write a short remark explaining the decision.
  5. Choose Update Availability. Available sends the request to the Reviewer.
Not Available ends the request

Marking funds Not Available denies the request; it does not come back to this queue. The requestor needs to file a new request once funds are in place.

The sub-account must hold the money itself

Only sub-accounts appear in the voucher's account list, and each one is checked against its own balance — a sub-account does not draw on the balance of the main account above it. If the list is empty, or the balance is short, an administrator needs to create the sub-account and post a deposit to it first (A3).

Your approving code

Every approval produces a ten-character approving code, shown once you submit and printed on the voucher from then on. It records that you personally cleared this request at that moment.

Stage 3

Review

Reviewer

Cleared requests arrive under Reviewer. Choose Review to see the request, its attachments and the voucher so far — the Fund Officer's code is already printed in the Prepared box.

  1. Read the remarks history, then set Decision: Approve moves the request to the Endorser; Send Back to Fund Availability returns it to the Fund Officer; Deny ends the request.
  2. Write your Remarks. They are required when you send the request back.
  3. Choose Save Review. Approving or denying gives you your own approving code.
Stage 4

Endorsement

Endorser

Reviewed requests appear under Endorsed By. This is the stage that decides who gives final approval, so read the request before choosing.

  1. Open the request with Endorse.
  2. Set Decision to Endorse, or to Send Back to Reviewer if something needs correcting first.
  3. When endorsing, use Choose Approver to pick the final approver — JCA or JMAPC. The request will appear only in that person's queue, and the dashboard lists will show it under Final Approver.
  4. Add your remarks (required when sending back) and choose Endorse Request, or Send Back.
Stage 5

Final approval

JCA or JMAPC Chair

Open Final Approval. Only the requests endorsed to you are listed. The voucher now carries three approving codes — prepared, checked and verified — so you can see who has already handled it and when.

  1. Choose Approve on the request. The Assigned Approver box confirms it was endorsed to you.
  2. Set Decision: Approve; Send Back to Endorser, which also clears the approver choice so the Endorser can choose again; or Deny, which ends the request.
  3. Add your remarks (required when sending back) and choose Submit Approval.

An approved request goes back to the Fund Officer for the voucher. No money has moved yet.

Stage 6

Prepare and print the voucher

Fund Officer

Approved requests wait under For Voucher. Choose Open Voucher to see the finished disbursement voucher, with the prepared, checked, verified and approved codes in place.

  1. Check the voucher against the approved request. Pay to, Address, Voucher No. and the particulars are the ones saved during the fund check (Stage 2); they cannot be changed here.
  2. Choose Print at the top right of the voucher card for the paper copy to be signed. Only the voucher prints, sized for a half sheet (8.5 × 5.5 in).
  3. Choose Download Excel beside it for the same voucher as a spreadsheet, laid out like the printed form.
Stage 7

Close the voucher

Fund Officer

When the money has actually been released, choose Complete/Close Voucher and confirm. This is the step that moves the money: the amount is deducted from the sub-account's ledger and the request becomes Completed.

This is the point of no return

Closing the voucher writes the deduction to the fund ledger. Do it when the disbursement has happened, not before.

Afterwards

Completed requests are listed under Completed, and View reopens the finished voucher — every approving code and timestamp in place, with the remarks history below it. Print and Download Excel at the top of the voucher card reprint or export it at any time.

Part III

The pages you use every day

Three screens sit outside the workflow but are available to everyone.

—

Your profile

Change your password, add a profile picture, and keep your name, position and birthdate current. Your name is what prints in the signature boxes of every voucher you approve, so it is worth getting right.

—

Attachments

Every file uploaded to a request you can see, in one list. Files are stored outside the public web folder and are served only after the system has checked your sign-in, so an attachment cannot be reached by guessing its address.

—

Reports

Filter requests by date, department, status or fund, then export the result. The ledger report shows every movement against a fund, with the request that caused it.

Part IV · Administrator only

Settings and records

Everything in this part lives under Admin Settings and is visible only to accounts with the Administrator role. The tabs are listed in the order you would need them when setting the system up for the first time.

A1

Manage users

Create an account for each person, give it a role and a department, and mark the department head where that applies. An account can be deactivated rather than deleted, which keeps its name on the vouchers it already approved.

One role per account

The role decides which queue a person sees and which stage they can act on. A person who needs to act at two stages needs two accounts.

A2

Manage departments

Create the departments that file requests and name the head of each. A requestor sees the requests of the department they belong to, so department membership is what decides who can read what.

A3

Source of fund

Funds have two levels. A main account is the heading — School Fund, Special Fund, Trust Fund. A sub-account sits under it and is what a voucher is actually charged to.

Set this up before anyone files a request

A Fund Officer can only mark funds available against a sub-account, and only if that sub-account's own balance covers the amount. Balances do not flow down from the main account. A main account with no sub-accounts cannot pay for anything.

Adding a sub-account

  1. Choose a main account to expand it.
  2. Type a Sub-Account Name and choose Add Sub-Account.

Posting a deposit

A new sub-account starts at zero. Choose View on it to open its ledger, then record the money it has been given.

  1. Enter the Deposit Amount and the date it was received.
  2. Add the OR, cheque or bank reference, and a short description.
  3. Choose Post Deposit. The amount is added to the balance and appears in the ledger below.
A4

Voucher approvers

The printed voucher has six signature boxes: prepared, checked, verified, recommending approval, approved, and the President. This tab sets the name and title printed in each one.

Where a real approval has been recorded, the person who actually gave it is printed instead, together with their approving code. The names set here fill the boxes that have no recorded approval — the President's box in particular, which is signed on paper.

A5

Branding

The credit line at the foot of every page. Leaving a field empty hides that part of it. The footer does not print on vouchers.

A6

Demo accounts and sample data

Two controls for the period before the system goes live.

Demo accounts on the sign-in page

While the tick box is on, the sign-in page lists the accounts in the box below it, passwords included, and anyone who opens that page can read them. Clearing the tick box removes the credentials from the page altogether — they are not merely hidden.

Turn this off before going live

On a public address this puts working passwords in front of anyone who finds the sign-in page.

Delete sample activity requests

Removes every activity request with its attachments, approvals and history, then empties the fund ledger so all balances read zero. Users, departments, fund accounts, voucher approvers and branding are kept. The button asks for confirmation and cannot be undone.

A7

Activity logs

Every sign-in, every approval, every administrative change, in order. Use it to answer who did what and when — including failed sign-in attempts, which is the first place to look if an account is locked out.

Screens in this handbook were captured from the working system while a single request — 20260911-SFXC-00001, ₱4,750.00 — was taken through all seven stages. The sign-in page and the request windows were refreshed on 15 September 2026 for the current layout, using the same sample request. Figures shown are sample data, not college records.
